newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian bolsa ends down as bank stocks fall.
newsitem.headline: Colombian bolsa ends down as bank stocks fall.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended down as banks fell in Bogota and cross deals between shareholders in one of the country's largest industrial conglomerates overwhelmed genuine supply and demand trends in Medellin.
Bogota's IBB index fell 0.17 percent to 828.84 in an 886.6 million peso volume. Medellin's IBOMED general price index dipped 0.07 percent to 13,202 in a 6.4 billion peso volume.
Brokers said growing fears that the United States could slap economic sanctions on Colombia if it does not introduce stiffer anti-drug laws failed to have any impact on the markets Thursday.
But they did not rule out the possibility of reaction in the future if U.S.-Colombian relations became more strained.
"In Bogota there was general market apathy because shareholders are loath to sell and foreign funds are being very demanding on prices," one Bogota broker said.
"We don't think political factors had any impact. Foreign funds are moving the markets. Today they didn't find packets that were big or cheap enough," another Bogota broker said.
In Bogota, Banco de Colombia fell 0.23 percent to 419 pesos, Banco de Bogota dropped 2.95 percent to 5,705 and Banco Industrial Colombiano dipped 0.03 percent to 3,300.
In Medellin, volume was concentrated in insurance company Suramericana de Seguros and chocolate manufacturer Compania Nacional de Chocolates -- both part of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno.

Suramericana rose 1.95 percent to 18,500 on a pre-arranged cross deal between exisiting shareholders while Nacional de Chocolates remained unchanged at 8,300 -- again the subejct of a pocket-to-pocket trade by existing shareholders.

"We estimate that only 5 percent of all Sindicato Antioqueno shares are in the hands of investors who are not actually partners in the conglomerate's member companies. That means that true supply is very limited and also opens the way for these huge cross deals," a Medellin dealer said.
